question.prompt: In triangle \(ABC,\) \(\angle C=\theta\) and \(\angle B=2\theta,\) where \(0^\circ\lt\theta\lt60^\circ.\) The circle with center \(A\) and radius \(AB\) intersects \(AC\) at \(D\) and intersects \(BC,\) extended if necessary, at \(B\) and at \(E\) (\(E\) may coincide with \(B\)). Then \(EC=AD\)

solutions.explanation:
Since \(AB\) and \(AD\) are radii, it is enough to prove \(CE=AB\). The given angles suggest constructing a triangle with two angles equal to \(\theta\).

Draw a ray from \(A\), on the same side of line \(AC\) as \(B\), making angle \(\theta\) with ray \(AC\). Let it meet ray \(CB\) at \(F\). The rays meet because their angles with the base \(AC\) sum to \(2\theta<180^\circ\). In triangle \(ACF\),
\[
\angle CAF=\angle ACF=\theta,
\]
so \(AF=CF\). We will show that \(AF=AB\), placing \(F\) on the given circle.

The original triangle has \(\angle CAB=180^\circ-3\theta\). There are three cases.

If \(0^\circ<\theta<45^\circ\), then \(180^\circ-3\theta>\theta\), so ray \(AF\) lies inside angle \(CAB\), and \(F\) lies between \(C\) and \(B\). Thus \(\angle ABF=2\theta\). Also \(\angle AFC=180^\circ-2\theta\), so its supplementary angle \(\angle AFB=2\theta\). Equal angles in triangle \(ABF\) give \(AF=AB\).

If \(45^\circ<\theta<60^\circ\), then \(180^\circ-3\theta<\theta\), so \(F\) lies beyond \(B\) on ray \(CB\). Now
\[
\angle ABF=180^\circ-2\theta
=\angle AFB,
\]
because rays \(FB\) and \(FC\) coincide. Again \(AF=AB\).

If \(\theta=45^\circ\), ray \(AF\) is ray \(AB\), so \(F=B\). Moreover, \(\angle ABC=90^\circ\), making line \(BC\) perpendicular to radius \(AB\) and hence tangent to the circle. Therefore \(E=B=F\).

In the first two cases, \(F\ne B\) is the other circle intersection, so \(F=E\) there as well. Consequently,
\[
CE=CF=AF=AB=AD
\]
throughout \(0^\circ<\theta<60^\circ\). The answer is choice E.
